recipes.name: Hollandaise Sauce
ingredients_raw: salt and ground white pepper to taste

steps.text: Whisk egg yolks in a small heavy saucepan until light lemon yellow and slightly thickened, about 1 minute. Whisk in1 to 1½ tablespoons lemon juice, depending on how tart you like your sauce.

Add 2 tablespoons cold butter to egg mixture. Place the pan over very low heat and whisk constantly until butter melts and mixture thickens enough to see the bottom of the pan between strokes. (If the mixture starts to thicken too quickly or look grainy, remove it from the heat and whisk in 1 teaspoon cold water.)
Remove the pan from heat. Whisk in remaining cold butter, 1 tablespoon at a time, until incorporated and smooth.

Gradually whisk in the melted butter, adding just a few drops at first, then a slow, steady stream. Keep whisking vigorously to create a thick, smooth sauce. (If sauce becomes too thick, whisk in 1 teaspoon warm water at a time until you reach the desired consistency.)
Season with salt and white pepper to taste. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Hollandaise Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This hollandaise sauce recipe is an easy, creamy classic sauce made à la minute for spooning over poached eggs benedict, grilled salmon, or veggies.

review.reviewBody: wonderful and easy! I've struggled with hollandaise sauce in the past and now those days are over. tip: to reheat leftovers, steam veggies and then put teaspoonfulls of hardened sauce (you can warm it to room temp) over steaming hot veggies and cover. In 5 minutes, the sauce is perfect, as if it were just made. If you microwave leftover sauce, it will separate.

I took other reviewers advice and used less butter than the recipe called for and a makeshift double boiler. I also used salted Kerrygold butter and skipped the step of adding salt. Instead of 3/4 cup of melted butter, I used a 1/4 cup instead. It seemed to be a much better combination. It seemed to be just enough. I can't imagine using the additional half cup. After making these adjustments to the recipe, it came out beautifully. It had just enough saltiness and acidity. I am going to have a difficult time eating hollandaise sauce elsewhere.

I cheated. Used microwave very cautiously. Was cooking for just me! Only used one yolk. Used a fork to keep it creamy by stopping microwave 10-15 seconds at a time. Was complete in no time!! Delishhhhhhh

I liked it! I used a double boiler to melt all the butter for a 1/2 batch...2 egg yolks, 1/2 stick butter. Once butter was melted I tempered the yolks with a little of the melted butter and then slowly added the yolks, constantly wisking. It started to separate but I added a few drops of warm water and it smoothed out perfectly. To finish I added two drops Worchesterhire sauce and a pinch of ground Cayene pepper. Great results.

The only problem with it, it makes too little! If entertaining or cooking for more then 2-4 I would double this recipe. 
If your sauce is breaking your are either not stirring constantly or your heat is too high. For the Hollandaise, you must stir constantly and vigorously with a wire whisk. This recipe requires our constant attention. You cannot leave it for a second. If you find it too sour reduce the lemon juice. Too salty, reduce the salt. If you don't like the black flecks of pepper, use a white pepper. It is up to you. You are the chef. That is what Allrecipes is all about.
NOTE: For high altitude I recommend reducing the butter and the lemon juice by 1/4.

If the sauce breaks, allow to cool and whisk in 1 tsp of cool water until it solidifies. Return to heat and continue cooking. Of course the best way to stop it from breaking is not to stop whisking from the time you put it on the heat and as soon as the butter is melted remove from the heat.

Excellent recipe, though I found that 1/2 tsp of white pepper more than enough. Otherwise it is overpowering. This goes well not only for eggs Benedict but also on asparagus and (might seem strange) steak.

I have had Hollandaise with lemon before but I prefer mine made with vinegar. I was taught by my father before whisks were available for home cooks. I stood at the stove with a flat saucepan over a simmering pot of water. I stirred the yolks with a fork till lemon yellow. Added the butter one drop (in the beginning) at a time till emulsified. It was wonderful. Now I put the eggs yolks (broken), salt, cayenne, vinegar in a jar and shake and shake and then add the warm butter. Then it's a question of how long you want to shake. Great on veggies, bread or even your finger.
I reduced the melted butter by half and still had a rich, lemony sauce. Delicious!

Turned out great!! I only needed one serving so I cut the recipe in thirds, but followed the dimensions exactly. It will vary depending on your eggs and your lemon, so you should taste it and add more or less butter depending on consistency. For me, it was perfect. I did use a double boiler however.
followed suggestion to use only 1/4 cup melted butter, which I thought was good and left texture right. step by step instructions were super helpful. I added a touch of Dijon.

This hollandaise actually came out better than expected, since the technique is a bit different than the traditional method. Everyone loved it, so no complaints. It was a bit loose, but I added a tablespoon of water before adding most of the melted butter because it seemed quite thick at the moment. Will make again!

It was great up until I added the melted butter. I think it might be a misprint? It was way too much and made my sauce all butter. I would say add the melted butter at your own discretion; definitely taste it before following the recipe fully.
Easy and turned out perfect

Outstanding! I've cooked brunch for years, and this recipe and method is considerably less fussy than commercial prep. I subbed cayenne pepper for white pepper, and used fresh lemon juice. Marvelous flavor! Thank you so much! NO MORE DOUBLE BOILERS LOL

Easiest hollandaise recipe I’ve ever used! I followed the ingredients and instructions exactly, and at the end when I wanted it a little thicker, I heated it and whisked until it reached the desired texture.

Very very good sauce, I used 4 yolks and squeezed half a lemon and it was amazing! I didn’t use English muffins instead I used slices of sourdough loaf bread toasted on the same griddle as my Canadian bacon. Definitely a keeper sauce

It tasted just great. BUT I didn't listen to the heat requirements and it ended up being too thin. I was so worried about it "curdleing" that I missed the need to heat it up pretty high. Ok, next time it will be better!
Tastes like straight butter
Wayyyy too lemony even with only 1 tbsp of juice. I used bottled lemon which likely didn't help, but I'd suggest starting with just a splash and then adding to taste.
Excellent flavor!
